title: close the chain-nudge registered-worker coverage gap and two conformance-honesty residuals left by rust-port-17
action: Fix-first cell closing what rust-port-17's rework round did not reach — the orchestrator's own omission when relaying the round-1 judge findings, not the worker's. THREE items, all inside crates/queen-bee. (1) THE REAL GAP: the cell action for rust-port-17 named the worker-collect nudge as firing 'when a bee worker OR swarming phase', but no fixture ever seeds state.workers (`rg workers crates/queen-bee/tests/heavyhooks_conformance.rs` returns nothing). Every nudge fixture triggers via phase=swarming only, so chain_nudge.rs:124 is_registered_worker and the whole ported worker_name() fallback ladder (chain_nudge.rs:62-77, mirroring bee-chain-nudge.mjs:36-47: string entry, then nickname|name|agent|worker) is never diffed against the frozen oracle. Seed state.workers fixtures covering EACH rung of that ladder plus the registered-worker-without-swarming-phase trigger, diffed byte-for-byte against the real mjs hook through the existing rig. Related and in scope: no chain-nudge fixture passes session_id, so state::resolve_pipeline (chain_nudge.rs:116, mjs :78) is never exercised — the phase always arrives via the readState fallback; add at least one fixture that pins a session id so the resolve_pipeline path is diffed too. (2) HONESTY RESIDUALS in the same target: three same-runtime before/after no-op assertions still compare parsed serde_json Values (heavyhooks_conformance.rs:603, :802-803, :861) — under this workspace's preserve_order feature an IndexMap's PartialEq ignores key order, so a rewrite that only reordered keys would pass; :861's message additionally CLAIMS 'byte-identical' while being key-order-blind. Convert them to the target's own assert_files_byte_equal_redacted (or make each message state exactly what it checks). (3) An unasserted argument: model_guard.rs:57 now passes its own hook name to run_fail_open, but modelguard_conformance.rs:569 calls run_fail_open directly with a literal, so a regression at that call site is caught by nothing — assert the model-guard crash line's hook field the way heavyhooks_conformance now does for chain-nudge and state-sync. RED-FIRST IS MANDATORY for every item: reintroduce each defect, quote the failure, revert, show green. Scratch space, if needed, is .bee/tmp/rust-port-21/ inside the worktree — never /tmp, which the write guard denies.

truths: at least one fixture per rung of the worker_name() fallback ladder (string entry, nickname, name, agent, worker) plus a registered-worker trigger that does not rely on phase=swarming, each diffed byte-for-byte against the real frozen bee-chain-nudge.mjs
at least one chain-nudge fixture pins a session id so state::resolve_pipeline is exercised rather than the readState fallback
no store-file or state comparison in heavyhooks_conformance.rs remains parsed-Value-based, and no assertion message claims a byte-level guarantee it does not provide
the model-guard crash line's hook field is asserted cross-runtime, so a regression at model_guard.rs:57 goes red
red-first evidence quoted for every item: the defect reintroduced, the exact failure, then green after revert

trace.outcome: Closed the chain-nudge registered-worker coverage gap and two conformance-honesty residuals rust-port-17's rework did not reach (orchestrator relay omission, not a worker miss). (1) Added worker_name() fallback-ladder fixtures (string/nickname/name/agent/worker, table-driven) + a no-match silence twin, plus a session-id fixture proving state::resolve_pipeline's lane branch drives the nudge. (2) Converted 3 same-runtime no-op assertions from parsed-Value to byte-level/raw-text comparisons; the LOCK_BUSY message's 'byte-identical' claim is now literally true. (3) Added a cross-runtime model-guard crash hook-field assertion that drives the REAL queen-bee hook model-guard dispatch (not a direct run_fail_open call with a literal), catching a regression at model_guard.rs:57. heavyhooks_conformance 16->19, modelguard_conformance 13->14. Zero production-behaviour changes (prohibition honored) -- every finding proved with red-first evidence.
deviations: Fix-first cell closing a coverage gap the round-1 judge raised but the
orchestrator did not relay in rust-port-17's rework round (per the
coordinator, not a worker miss). Three items, all proof-gap work, zero
production-behaviour changes:
1. Added fixtures for every rung of `worker_name()`'s fallback ladder
(string entry, then object entries matched via nickname/name/agent/
worker), table-driven per test-economy D3, plus a non-triviality twin
(an entry matching no rung stays silent) — none of these previously
existed; every chain-nudge nudge fixture up to this cell triggered via
`phase=swarming` only. Also added a fixture pinning a real `session_id`
bound to a lane whose own record carries `phase=swarming` while the
default `state.json` stays idle, proving `state::resolve_pipeline`'s
lane branch — not the `readState` fallback — decides the nudge.
2. Converted the three same-runtime before/after no-op assertions the cell
named (disabled-hook, throttled-no-op, LOCK_BUSY) from parsed
`serde_json::Value` comparisons to raw-text comparisons — under this
workspace's `preserve_order` feature an `IndexMap`'s `PartialEq` ignores
key order, so these were silently blind to a reordering rewrite; the
LOCK_BUSY assertion's message additionally claimed "byte-identical"
while being exactly the opposite. The message now matches the check.
3. Added a cross-runtime crash-line assertion for model-guard
(`crash_fail_open_both_runtimes_log_the_correct_hook_name`), driving
BOTH runtimes through their real crash paths — critically, the rust
side through the actual `queen-bee hook model-guard` dispatch (a new
`run_rust_with_crash_seam` helper), never a direct call to the shared
`run_fail_open` wrapper with a hand-supplied literal (the existing
`crash_fail_open_rust_wrapper_...` test does that, which proves the
wrapper but not model_guard.rs's own call site) — so a regression at
`model_guard.rs:57` is now caught.
Red-first evidence for all four sub-items (the two halves of item 1, item
2, and item 3) is in this cap's `verification_evidence` (`red_failure_evidence`
field) and the report — each defect was genuinely reintroduced in the real
source (or, for item 2, demonstrated on real session-shaped data via a
scratch experiment that was run and then removed, never shipped), the
affected test's failure quoted, then reverted to green.
No production files were touched — confirmed via `git diff --stat
crates/queen-bee/src/` after every red-first revert.
